chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Dailami, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying:
The winter is the spring of the believer; its night is prolonged, so he uses it to stand (in prayer), and its day is shortened, so he uses it to fast.

key_terms.ربيع: Spring (metaphorically, a season of growth and vitality)
key_terms.قيام: Standing in prayer, specifically night prayer (qiyam al-layl)

ai.seo_question: Why is winter considered the spring of the believer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) metaphorical identification of winter as the believer's 'spring,' emphasizing the strategic advantage of extended nights for *qiyam al-layl* and abbreviated days for *sawm*. This tradition reflects the Shia emphasis on utilizing natural rhythms for spiritual elevation, linking the physical ease of fasting in cooler weather with the devotion of night prayers. It underscores the holistic view of worship where environmental conditions are leveraged to deepen one's connection with the Divine.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammed bin Ahmad bin Yahya bin Imran al-Ash’ari, from Ibrahim bin Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from Muhammed bin Sulayman al-Dailami, from his father, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said: I heard him saying:
The winter is the spring of the believer. Its night is prolonged with him, so he uses it to stand (in prayer), and its day is shortened, so he uses it to fast.
